Hush, Little Baby in Irish and English

In Irish it is Fuist, a Linbh. Here are the words in both languages, side by side, with a gentle tune to sing along to.

Sing along in Irish Sing along in English

The words light up as the tune plays. No microphone, nothing to sign up for.

Fuist, a Linbh (Irish)

Fuist, a linbh, téigh a chodladh anois,
gheobhaidh Daidí éinín beag duit.

Is mura gcanann an t-éinín beag,
gheobhaidh Daidí fáinne óir duit.

Is má chailltear an fáinne óir,
gheobhaidh Daidí scáthán beag duit.

Is má bhriseann an scáthán beag,
gheobhaidh Daidí gabhar beag duit.

Hush, Little Baby (English)

Hush, little baby, don't say a word,
Papa's gonna buy you a mockingbird.

And if that mockingbird don't sing,
Papa's gonna buy you a diamond ring.

And if that diamond ring turns brass,
Papa's gonna buy you a looking glass.

And if that looking glass gets broke,
Papa's gonna buy you a billy goat.

About the song

Words and tune: traditional American lullaby, 19th century, author unknown. Tune as in the public-domain score and MIDI on Wikimedia Commons ("Hush, Little Baby", traditional; setting by Peter Gerloff, CC0), transposed from G to C. Public domain.

The Irish words were written for Calm Match to fit the same tune, one syllable to each note. They are still being checked by a fluent Irish speaker, so they may change. Spotted something to improve? Email hello@calmmatch.com.
